summary: Jiayao An is an archaeologist and Sinologist who studied under Su Bai from circa 1978 to 1982. Around 1982, she was appointed special researcher and director of the Xi'an Research Office at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.

Jiayue Kang works in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. Kang completed graduate studies at East China Normal University (1996–2001), earned an MA in Sanskrit at Silpakorn University (2022–2025), and held a post at Silpakorn University.

Sinologist and historian Jiegang Gu studied at Peking University (ca. 1913–1920) under Taiyan Zhang and Hu Shih. He later held posts at Peking University, Fudan University, the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.
Jien Abe was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed graduate studies at the University of Tokyo (attested 1973). He served as a professor at Meiji University until 2001.

Jifu Lan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Tunghai University (ca. 1965–1969) and served as a full-time researcher at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies from circa 1985 until retiring in 2019.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Jigdal Dagchen Sakya studied under Ngawang Thutop Wangchuk, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He held a post at the University of Washington from circa 1960 to 1969.

Jigme Chhoeda, a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar, studied at Druk Sangag Choeling and Tango monasteries under teachers including Dudjom Rinpoche. He served as Abbot of Tango Monastery and Drapoi Lopen, later becoming Dorji Lopen in 1995.
Jigme Pema Wangchen is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Dzi Gar Khenpo Nor Yang, Drukpa Khenpo Ngawang Chödrak, and Mi-pham-bśad-sgrub-chos-kyi-ñin-byed-mchog.
Jigme Tenpai Nyima studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He was also a teacher to Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Jigmeth Junu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University (attested 2013) under supervisor Yongdong Shi, having also studied under traditional teacher Hui Xian.
Jikai Fujiyoshi was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Rissho University and was attested as a member at Kyoto University in 1967.

Jikido Takasaki was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned doctorates at Savitribai Phule Pune University and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Komazawa, Osaka, and Tokyo universities, and served as president of Tsurumi Women's University.

Jim G. Shaffer is an archaeologist and Indologist. He earned a BA at Arizona State University (ca. 1961–1965), a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (ca. 1966–1972), and was an anthropology professor at Case Western Reserve University (ca. 1972–2010).

Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar Jim Rheingans earned an MA at the University of Hamburg and a PhD through the University of the West of England and Bath Spa University. He has held posts at Hamburg, Vienna, and Sydney.

Jin Kyoung Choi works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Choi studied for a doctorate and served as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University, and is attested as a lecturer at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

Jin Y. Park is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. Park served as an assistant professor of philosophy and religion at American University (attested 2007–2012) and as a visiting fellow at City University of Hong Kong.
Jin-il Chung is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. Chung has served as a staff member (attested 2008) and editor (attested 2026) at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Jinah Kim, an art historian, Indologist, and Buddhist studies scholar, earned a PhD at UC Berkeley under Joanna Gottfried Williams. She held posts at Vanderbilt University and the Institute for Advanced Study, and is a professor at Harvard University.
Jinavijaya Muni was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He served as principal of Gujarat Vidyapith and founded the Rajasthan Puratana Granthamala (attested 1959).

Jinbo Shi is a scholar of history, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Minzu University and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences under Jingru Wang, he held posts at CASS, Minzu University, North Minzu University, and Ningxia University.
